lead: Machinery and equipment for farms, smallholdings, woodlands and apiaries, from compact and vintage tractors to implements, harvest, livestock, forestry and beekeeping gear, organised by job; production machines stay at kind level, while vintage tractors, stationary engines and beehives are mapped to named archetypes.

b.m: Power and fit to the job
b.w: Measured PTO and drawbar power against the job, plus hitch category and which implements fit; fit to the job comes first.
Measured in the Nebraska (OECD) tractor test.
Owner surveys put dealer support first.

b.v: gear / shuttle < powershift < hydrostatic or CVT (for convenience)
b.w: Hydrostatic dominates sub-compact and compact; CVT at the top of farm ranges.
Cab, air conditioning and sound level are compared in tests.
Matched to the work, not a ladder.

k.a: sub-compact utility tractor · SCUT · garden compact
k.d: Smallest true tractor, under about 25 hp, with a three-point hitch, four-wheel drive and a mid-mount mower deck, sold to homeowners.
Scaled-down farm tractor of roughly 25–60 hp with rear and mid PTO, three-point hitch and usually a front loader, for acreage and estate work.
General-purpose wheeled tractor of roughly 60–120 hp with rear PTO and three-point hitch, used to pull, carry and drive implements on small farms.

k.a: walking tractor · walk-behind tractor · single-axle tractor · pedestrian tractor · hand tractor · power tiller · motoculteur · iron buffalo
k.d: Single-axle tractor with a PTO that drives or pulls interchangeable implements, the operator walking behind or riding a towed implement.
Wheeled tractor with adjustable track and clearance for working between crop rows.
Large tractor with four equal driven wheels that steers by bending at a central pivot.
Tractor running on two full-length tracks, steel or rubber, instead of wheels.
Tractor running on four separate track units, one at each corner, on an articulated or rigid frame.
Tractor with front tyres and rear crawler tracks.

k.a: narrow tractor · tracteur fruitier · tracteur vigneron · Schmalspurtraktor
k.d: Wheeled tractor with a narrow track and low profile for working between vines and fruit trees.
Tractor with high ground clearance that straddles rows of vines or crops.
Low, wide tractor with a low centre of gravity that carries mowers and implements on steep ground.
Wheeled tractor built and guarded for forest work such as winching and skidding; also shown under Forestry.
Self-propelled carrier that carries and drives implements, with no load body; a Unimog with a load bed is in Vehicles.

depts.note: Current tractors at kind level; sizes from sub-compact to articulated. Vintage tractors have their own department.

b.v: restored to original spec > period-correct > modified
b.w: Club and show judging standards; serial-number dating.
Popular archetypes (TE20, Ford N, Farmall, Lister) are fully supported by reproduction parts.

k.a: pioneer tractor · kerosene tractor · prairie tractor
k.d: Petrol- or kerosene-burning farm tractor from the first decades of the internal-combustion tractor, before about 1930.

IH's large petrol tractors, sold as Mogul by McCormick dealers and Titan by Deering dealers.

v.d: first important IH tractors with the 10-20

Italian single-cylinder two-stroke semi-diesel tractors, made from the first 1925 prototype until 1957.

k.a: hit 'n' miss engine · flywheel engine · farm engine
k.d: Slow-running flywheel engine whose governor holds the exhaust valve open and skips firing above a set speed.

v.d: sold under this name by September 1897

v.d: fitted to Cadbury's Bournville I and II

k.a: thresher · threshing drum · separator · thrashing machine

Ipswich-built threshing drum made from about 1841 alongside portable and traction engines.

Reaper that cuts grain and ties it into sheaves, driven by a bull-wheel; invented by Charles Withington.

Machine that removes the husk from paddy rice.
